findings.title: Hard-coded Portuguese user-facing sentences built inside Providers wire types/providers; the matching localized keys are dead
findings.evidence: GeminiWireTypes.swift:57/71/136 disclaimer: "Para conseguir monitorar o Gemini, ... Antigravity instalado e autenticado."; XAIWireTypes.swift:251 defaultDisclaimer = "Para conseguir monitorar o Grok, ..."; GeminiProvider.swift:81,103,106 and XAIProvider.swift:118 throw AppError.credentials/io with Portuguese text; AntigravityExecutor.swift:58,162,174 likewise. VendorSectionView.swift:655-660 renders Text(disclaimer) verbatim. en/es/pt-BR Localizable.strings define gemini_antigravity_disclaimer and xai_grok_disclaimer, but no Swift file references either key.
findings.impact: Violates the CLAUDE.md rule: Never build a user-facing sentence inside a wire type; emit structure and let the localized view render it. That rule was written after a pt-BR card showed English; this is the same bug in reverse. Every en/es user with Gemini or Grok enabled sees a Portuguese info line on each card, and Portuguese error text when a credential is missing. Because the Snapshot contract carries prose instead of structure, the App cannot localize it.
findings.fix: Replace disclaimer: String? on GeminiSnapshot/XAISnapshot with a structured flag/enum (requiresAntigravity / requiresGrokCLI) resolved in the view via the existing L10n keys; model credential-missing errors as typed AppError cases localized by the view; update golden tests.

test_red_green.name: ProvidersEmitNoNaturalLanguageTests.no_portuguese_literals + GoldenSnapshotTests.gemini_disclaimer_is_structured
test_red_green.assert_before: A source scan of Sources/AiTaskbarProviders for Para conseguir / Para monitorar finds matches, and GeminiSnapshot.disclaimer is a Portuguese String: FAIL
test_red_green.assert_after: No matches; the snapshot exposes a Bool/enum, and a view test resolves it to the en string under languageOverride=en

findings.cetico_evidence: Duplicate of CQ-AUR-001 (same literals and render sites: VendorSectionView.swift:655-660, 724-729). Merge them. The structural fix (flag/enum in the snapshot) is the one consistent with CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: UsageWindow.label is both English display text and the identity key; Anthropic scoped vs flat Opus (7d) can collide despite a comment claiming dedupe
findings.evidence: AnthropicWireTypes.swift:161-166 seeds var seenScoped = Set<String>() only with scoped labels (label = name + " (7d)"), yet the comment says it dedupes a scoped Opus against seven_day_opus. Line 195 separately emits opus: window(seven_day_opus, label: "Opus (7d)"); UsageSnapshot.swift:44-46 concatenates scoped + opus into windows. Consumers key on label: VendorSectionView.swift:557 ForEach(snap.windows, id: label keypath); NotificationService.swift:71 key = vendor:label, and the request identifier at :107.
findings.impact: If the API returns seven_day_opus together with a weekly_scoped entry whose display_name is Opus, the result is duplicate SwiftUI ForEach ids (rows dropped or mis-diffed) and two windows sharing one notification-dedupe slot, so alerts re-fire whenever the two percentages alternate. Tying identity to English prose also blocks localizing labels without breaking dedupe.
findings.fix: Seed seenScoped with the flat labels, or better, add a stable id to UsageWindow, use it for ForEach and notification keys, and keep label display-only.

test_red_green.name: AnthropicGoldenTests.scoped_opus_does_not_duplicate_flat_opus
test_red_green.assert_before: A fixture with seven_day_opus plus weekly_scoped display_name Opus yields windows with Opus (7d) twice; Set(labels).count != labels.count: FAIL

findings.cetico_evidence: The mismatch is real: AnthropicWireTypes.swift:159-167 claims to dedupe a scoped 'Opus' against seven_day_opus, but seenScoped is seeded only with scoped labels, and :195 emits 'Opus (7d)' separately. The only observed payload scopes 'Fable' (Fixtures.swift:9,15-17), so the triggering input (seven_day_opus plus a weekly_scoped Opus) is unobserved.

findings.title: VendorViewModel hard-binds the real on-disk UsageHistoryStore and UserDefaults.standard, so the vendor refresh path has zero tests
findings.evidence: VendorViewModel.swift:144 reads UserDefaults.standard for the expansion key; :146 self.historyStore = try? UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(provider.vendorId), which resolves to ~/Library/Application Support/ai-taskbar/history (UsageHistoryStore.swift:34-38). refresh() (:214) calls recordHistory (:235, :274-276 store.append). AnalyticsStore.swift:203 separately constructs UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(vendor). Tests build VendorViewModel 15 times (e.g. PinnedStatusItemTests.swift:103), but none calls vm.refresh or UsageStore.refreshAll. The only refreshAll calls in Tests are on ServiceStatusStore.
findings.impact: The core per-vendor flow (loading to ok/failed, stale handling, the per-vendor 429 cooldown that scheduler back-off depends on, history recording, notification trigger) cannot be exercised without appending samples to the real user history JSONL, so it is untested. App is also outside the coverage gate.
findings.fix: Inject historyStore and defaults into VendorViewModel.init, built at the composition root (AiTaskbarApp.init / AppEnvironment); have AnalyticsStore read VendorViewModel.historyStore instead of constructing new instances.

test_red_green.name: VendorViewModelRefreshTests.rate_limited_refresh_sets_cooldown_and_records_no_history
test_red_green.assert_before: No seam to supply a temp-dir history store; a refresh test would write into the real Application Support path
test_red_green.assert_after: VendorViewModel(provider: Mock429, historyStore: tmpStore, defaults: suite).refresh gives a failed + isRateLimited state; tmpStore.load() is empty

findings.cetico_evidence: VendorViewModel.swift:143-145 hard-binds UserDefaults.standard and UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(real path). No test calls VendorViewModel.refresh (the only refreshAll calls are ServiceStatusAppTests.swift:119,195,219). Downgraded: this is a missing test seam in the App target, which is excluded from the coverage gate by policy. No behavior defect is shown.

findings.title: UpdateChecker gets a fresh default HTTPClient instead of env.http, contradicting its own pinned comment
findings.evidence: AiTaskbarApp.swift:21 let updates = UpdateChecker(config: env.config.updates). UpdateChecker.swift:66 defaults http: HTTPClient = .init(). UpdateChecker.swift:243-244 comment: Route through the injected HTTPClient (pinned/ephemeral), never URLSession.shared. AppEnvironment.swift:30-36 builds the pinned client only into env.http.
findings.impact: Any pin_hosts entry that covers the GitHub release/asset hosts is silently ignored for the update check and DMG download. The composition root security policy does not reach this consumer, and the comment claims it does. Mitigated by size/SHA256 checks when the release provides them.
findings.fix: Pass http: env.http in AiTaskbarApp.init, or remove the default parameter so omission fails to compile.

test_red_green.name: CompositionRootTests.update_checker_uses_environment_http
test_red_green.assert_before: Source scan: AiTaskbarApp.swift constructs UpdateChecker without http: FAIL
test_red_green.assert_after: UpdateChecker.init has no default http; call site passes env.http

findings.cetico_evidence: AiTaskbarApp.swift:21 calls UpdateChecker(config:) without http:, so it gets the default HTTPClient() (UpdateChecker.swift:65). env.http is pinned only when pin_hosts is set (AppEnvironment.swift:30-37). The comment at UpdateChecker.swift:243-244 claims the injected pinned client is used. Only matters if a user pins GitHub hosts.

findings.title: UsageStore.togglePinned calls the AppKit singleton PinnedStatusItemManager.shared; the geometry-denial branch is untestable through the store
findings.evidence: UsageStore.swift:244 PinnedStatusItemManager.shared.canAddPinnedStatusItem(...). PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:343 guard let store, let screen = NSScreen.screens.first else { return .allowedResult }; the manager also holds the store via configure(store:) at :165, so the reference is bidirectional. PinnedStatusItemTests.swift:134-168 pass only because shared.store is nil in tests, which takes the allowed path.
findings.impact: The store-level integration of the notch/space limit, which took four fix PRs (#26-#29), cannot be tested: tests always see allowed, and a configured manager would read the live menu bar of the test machine. The pure evaluateSpaceMath is tested; its wiring into togglePinned is not.
findings.fix: Inject a pinSpaceChecker closure/protocol into UsageStore, defaulted at the composition root to PinnedStatusItemManager.shared.canAddPinnedStatusItem.

test_red_green.name: UsageStorePinTests.toggle_respects_denied_space_check
test_red_green.assert_before: No way to make togglePinned see a denied geometry result without a live screen
test_red_green.assert_after: With a checker that always denies, togglePinned(.openai) leaves pinnedVendorIds empty and sets pinLimitAlert

findings.cetico_evidence: UsageStore.swift:244 calls PinnedStatusItemManager.shared directly. It returns allowed when no store or screen is configured, so the denied branch cannot be reached from store-level tests.

findings.title: CachedFetch fresh-cache decode failure escapes the lifecycle (no network retry, no markFailed)
findings.evidence: CachedFetch.swift:26-30 if !forceRefresh, let hit = cache.freshPayloadWithAge() { return try makeOutcome(from: hit.0, decode: decode, ...) } sits outside the do/catch, so a decode throw on cached bytes propagates straight to the caller.
findings.impact: When a decoder changes on upgrade (e.g. the XAICachedPayload envelope or the Gemini schema-throwing branch), a still-fresh cache entry makes each tick fail for up to the TTL (~5 min) without trying the network. last_error is not recorded, so the stale tooltip cannot explain it. It self-heals, so impact is limited.
findings.fix: On a fresh-hit decode failure, discard the entry and fall through to fetch, inside CachedFetch (extend, do not fork).

test_red_green.name: CachedFetchTests.fresh_undecodable_cache_falls_through_to_fetch
test_red_green.assert_before: Seed a fresh cache with bytes that make decode throw and a fetch that returns valid bytes: run() throws
test_red_green.assert_after: run() returns the fetched snapshot with isStale false and overwrites the cache

findings.cetico_evidence: CachedFetch.swift:26-30: the fresh-hit makeOutcome/decode sits outside the do/catch at :31-64, so there is no fetch fallthrough and no markFailed. Reachability is narrow: the cache is written only after a successful decode (:34-36), so it takes a decoder change across an upgrade within the TTL. It self-heals within ~5 min.

findings.title: Flame severity color rule duplicated in 3 places and diverging from SeverityColor
findings.evidence: MenuBarLabelView.swift:48 and :80 (percent >= store.thresholds.critical || percent >= 100) ? Color.red : Color.orange; PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:86 repeats it; ColorTheme.swift:11-12 maps >=100 to red and >=critical to orange.
findings.impact: Between critical and 99% the flame is red while the adjacent icon is orange. The rule is copied three times, so a threshold change must be made in all of them. Cosmetic.
findings.fix: Add SeverityColor.flame(forPercent:thresholds:) and use it at all three sites.

test_red_green.name: SeverityColorTests.flame_band
test_red_green.assert_before: Rule is inline in the views; nothing to assert
test_red_green.assert_after: The shared helper is pinned for the critical..99 band

findings.cetico_evidence: MenuBarLabelView.swift:48,80 and PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:86 each repeat `>= critical || >= 100 ? red : orange`. ColorTheme.swift:11-12 maps >=100 to red and >=critical to orange. The two rules diverge in the critical..99 band.
